artists.biography:
How to Destroy Angels (stylized How to destroy angels_) is a musical group featuring Nine Inch Nails frontman Trent Reznor, his wife Mariqueen Maandig, Atticus Ross, and Rob Sheridan (who is also the group's art director). The group is named after a 1984 Coil single of the same name.

The band's first release was a self-titled EP, released on June 1, 2010. The band released a track from the album, "A Drowning", as a digital single, and a second song, "The Space in Between", debuted as a video on Pitchfork on May 14, 2010. A third track, "The Believers", was made available through Wired magazine's iPad application, along with a dissection and analysis of the song, and through a free digital download from the official website. "The Believers" is also featured on the soundtrack of the 2011 film Limitless.

perplexity.description:
Welcome Oblivion is the debut studio album by How to Destroy Angels, released on March 5, 2013 through Columbia Records. The project, featuring Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and Mariqueen Maandig, presents a cohesive exploration of post-industrial electronic rock. Described by the Los Angeles Times as "sensual electronic rock," the album synthesizes experimental production with structured songwriting, drawing from the band's earlier EPs while establishing a distinct sonic identity separate from Reznor's work with Nine Inch Nails.

The album's conceptual framework, as articulated by designer Rob Sheridan, addresses "anxiety of information overload as humanity and technology converge," positioning technological singularity and post-humanism as simultaneously terrifying and transformative forces. This thematic underpinning informs the album's atmospheric yet propulsive sound, blending ambient textures with rhythmic electronic elements. The vinyl edition features two additional tracks—"The Province of Fear" and "Unintended Consequences"—alongside a slightly altered track sequence, while the deluxe digital edition incorporates the band's self-titled EP as bonus material.

Commercially, Welcome Oblivion achieved moderate chart success, reaching number 30 on the US Billboard 200 and number 8 on the Alternative Songs chart, while also charting at number 2 on the US Dance chart. The album received mixed critical reception, with SPIN magazine awarding it a 6 out of 10. The band supported the release with a North American tour in spring 2013, featuring innovative stage production utilizing LED light installations controlled in real-time during performances.
